chief_complaint: right upper quadrant pain after eating fatty foods
hpi_details: 50F presents with recurrent right upper quadrant pain radiating to the right shoulder, starting 1 hour after eating a hamburger. Pain lasts 2-3 hours. Denies fever or jaundice.

core_concepts: Pain is due to transient gallstone obstruction of the cystic duct.
common_misconceptions: Confusing with cholecystitis (which has fever/constant pain).
dangerous_errors: Missing cholangitis if jaundice is present.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.objective: Afebrile. Mild RUQ tenderness, negative Murphy sign.

learning_objectives: Differentiate biliary colic from acute cholecystitis.

teaching.one_liner: Episodic right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals, typical of symptomatic cholelithiasis without acute inflammation.

must_ask.say: Does the pain come on after eating fatty or greasy food?
Does the pain spread anywhere, like to your right shoulder or back?
How long does each episode of pain last, and does it go away completely afterward?
Have you had any fever or chills with these episodes?
Have you noticed yellowing of your skin or eyes, or dark urine?

history.answer: My right upper belly started hurting badly after I ate lunch, especially after eating greasy food.
The pain started suddenly about an hour after I had lunch today.
The pain is in the upper right part of my belly, and it has stayed right there the whole time.
Yes, it shoots through to my right shoulder blade and the right side of my back.
It feels like a deep, heavy cramp that squeezes and aches steadily.
It got up to about a seven out of ten at its worst, but it is slowly easing off now.
These attacks usually last for about two to three hours before fading away completely.
Eating fatty or fried foods triggers the pain, while sitting still and waiting it out helps it settle down.
I have had a couple of similar episodes over the past few months after eating fried chicken.
I felt quite nauseous when the pain peaked, but I never threw up.
My bowel movements have been completely normal, with no diarrhea, constipation, or dark blood.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or sweating.
No, my skin and eyes look normal, and my urine and stools are their usual color.
No, I do not have any pain with urination, urgency, or blood in my urine.
No, I haven't felt dizzy or lightheaded, and I have not passed out.
No, I have not noticed any abnormal vaginal bleeding or unusual discharge.
No, I do not have any chest pain, heart flutter, or shortness of breath.
I ate a greasy fast-food hamburger about an hour before the pain began, but I have not had any alcohol.
No, I have not taken any pain medications, aspirin, or anti-inflammatory pills.
No, I have never been diagnosed with heart rhythm problems or vascular disease.
A coworker who had similar symptoms said it sounded like gallstones, so I wondered if that might be it.
I am very worried that this agonizing pain will keep coming back every time I eat.
I came in hoping to get an ultrasound to find out what is causing this.
I have had issues with my weight, but I do not have high blood pressure, diabetes, or any other medical problems.
I had a normal vaginal delivery years ago, but I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I do not take any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or vitamins.
No, I do not have any known drug allergies.
I have never smoked in my life.
I do not drink alcohol, aside from maybe a glass of wine on rare occasions.
I work as an office clerk and live at home with my husband and two children.
My mother had surgery to remove her gallbladder when she was in her fifties, but there is no other major illness.
My last period ended two weeks ago and my cycles are regular, so there is no possibility of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, pulse is 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.8 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Sclerae are non-icteric and conjunctivae are pink without pallor.
Abdomen is mildly distended with adipose tissue, symmetrical, with no surgical scars or visible masses.
Normal active bowel sounds are present in all four quadrants with no bruits.
Mild tenderness is elicited upon deep palpation of the right upper quadrant, with no involuntary guarding or rigidity.
No rebound tenderness is present in any abdominal quadrant.
No inspiratory arrest upon deep palpation of the right subcostal region, confirming a negative Murphy sign.
No tenderness at McBurney point, and psoas and obturator signs are negative.
No tenderness to percussion over either costovertebral angle.
Normal sphincter tone with no rectal masses, tenderness, or visible blood.
